body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-29 end to end against the running dev instance (cwn-local, config_anonbrowse=1,
Guest carrying ROLE_ANONYMOUS), then fully reverted.

    1. BEFORE                      anonymous sees 51   guest membership rows 0
    2. POST /api/v1/admin/my-library/migrate {"user_id": 2}
       -> {"name":"Guest","status":"switched","seeded_books":51,"library_mode":"personal_library"}
    3. AFTER                       anonymous sees 51   guest rows 51   <- day one unchanged, as designed
    4. one book dropped from Guest's set
                                   anonymous sees 50   <- membership scoping DOES apply to anonymous
    5. Guest back to monolibrary   anonymous sees 51   <- reversible

The admin action is `migrateAll` in frontend/src/pages/Admin.tsx:163, whose confirmation reads
"Set up My Library for every user? Each account switches to its own selection after it is filled with
everything that account can currently see. Accounts set up before are never reseeded." It calls the
endpoint with NO user_id, and cps/api/admin.py:101 then selects every row in `user` with no
anonymous exclusion. cps/user_library.py migrate_users_to_personal_library() has none either.

WHY IT MATTERS. Guest is the account anonymous visitors browse as. After the bulk action, the
server's PUBLIC view is a curated membership set rather than the library. Day one is invisible
because the seed contains everything Guest could already see, which is exactly what makes it easy to
miss. From then on:

  * a newly added or uploaded book does NOT appear to anonymous visitors until someone puts it in
    Guest's library;
  * Guest cannot fix this itself - it cannot log in, so it can never use the self-service mode
    switch or the Global Library "add to my library" control;
  * the only remedies are the admin per-user mode control or
    PUT /api/v1/admin/users/2/my-library/<book_id>, neither of which an admin has any reason to look
    for, because nothing appears broken.

NOT A BUG IN THE MECHANISM. A Guest in personal-library mode using its own membership set is
deliberate and pinned by test_my_library_backend_1939.py::test_anonymous_browse_guest_uses_its_
membership_set. An administrator may legitimately want a curated public shelf, and this is the
feature that provides it. The defect is that the bulk action does it SILENTLY: "every user" is
literally true and the consequence for the public catalogue is not stated, so the admin most likely
to click it - one setting the feature up for the first time - is the one least likely to predict it.

FIX SHAPE, either is defensible and it is a product decision:
  (a) exclude anonymous accounts from the unscoped bulk migrate, and let an admin switch Guest
      deliberately via the existing per-user control; or
  (b) keep including it, name it in the confirmation, and report it distinctly in the result banner
      ("...including the public Guest account, so new books will not appear to signed-out visitors
      until you add them").

Prefer (a): the bulk action's purpose is to move real people onto the feature, and the public
catalogue is a separate decision with a different blast radius. (b) alone still leaves the admin one
mis-read confirmation away from freezing their public catalogue.

Only reachable when anonymous browsing is enabled (config_anonbrowse=1). Fully reversible: switching
Guest back to monolibrary restored anonymous visibility immediately.

resolution.note: Unscoped bulk migration now skips and reports anonymous accounts; explicitly scoped anonymous migration remains supported and idempotent.

title: 'Set up My Library for all users' silently includes the anonymous Guest account, freezing the server's public catalogue
